headline: SOLSTICE MINERALS NANADIE DELIVERS 10m @ 9.40% CU INSIDE 41m @ 2.79% CU — RESOURCE AVERAGE JUST 0.4%; GRADE 23X DEPOSIT MEAN
snippet: Solstice Minerals (ASX: SLS) reported hole NANRC067 at its Nanadie copper-gold project in WA's Murchison region cut 41 metres grading 2.79% copper and 0.70 g/t gold from 19 metres depth, including a high-grade core of 10 metres at 9.40% copper — a grade 23x the project's current resource average of 0.4% Cu across 40.4 million tonnes. The shallow depth (19m start) and exceptional high-grade core narrow cost assumptions significantly, and combined with prior wide-interval results including a 722m deep intercept at 0.44% Cu, reinforce Nanadie as a multi-style copper system with both shallow high-grade and larger lower-grade bulk-tonnage potential. For ASX copper investors, a 10m @ 9.4% Cu near-surface result in the Murchison is among the strongest copper drill intercepts of the Australian exploration season; shares moved sharply higher on the announcement.

headline: GOLD RALLIES NEARLY $75 TO ~$3,950 BEFORE MIDTERMS — WORST 8-WEEK PRE-VOTE LOSS IN 5 CYCLES; GOLD ROSE AFTER EACH OF LAST 4 MIDTERMS
snippet: A November 2 BullionVault analysis frames Monday's ~$75 spot gold recovery to ~$3,948/oz — driven by oil falling 6%+ on a third consecutive day of Iran-Qatar back-channel peace talks — in the context of the steepest pre-midterms decline in at least five election cycles: gold has shed 11.0% over the 8 weeks preceding Tuesday's vote. The historical pattern: gold rose over the following 8-week period after each of the past four US midterm elections. BullionVault notes this pre-vote loss is being driven by a combination of higher oil prices, tech-sector margin calls, and Fed hawkishness — but that every previous midterm cycle showing a comparable pre-vote correction showed outsized recoveries in the 60-day window after the vote. For retail investors, the article identifies this setup as the most historically compelling 8-week entry window in gold since 2018, while carefully avoiding a directional prediction.

headline: COUNTDOWN: CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT PAUSE EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 — 8 DAYS TO MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SUPPLY CHAIN DECISION OF 2026
snippet: A Yahoo Finance analysis confirms the countdown: China's October 2025 rare earth export control suspension — which covers products containing as little as 0.1% Chinese-origin rare earth content — expires November 10, 2026, with diplomatic talks still unresolved. The April 2025 controls on seven medium and heavy rare earths remain in force regardless. Analysts note persistent supply concentration: China holds ~55–70% of global mining and ~90% of midstream refining capacity. The suspension was widely read as a bargaining chip in US-China trade talks; a non-renewal would require foreign manufacturers using Chinese REE inputs to obtain MOFCOM case-by-case export licences — affecting companies across the downstream defence, EV and clean-energy sectors. The November 10 date is either the trigger for one of 2026's largest supply-chain disruptions or a signal that Beijing extends the pause again. Mining investors with positions in Lynas (ASX: LYC), Iluka (ASX: ILU), Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU), and MP Materials (NYSE: MP) need to position before the expiry.

headline: COPPERCORP (TSXV: CPER) WRAPS JUKES DRILLING — 12m @ 0.54% CU; TASMANIA AWARDS A$100K GOVERNMENT DRILLING GRANT
snippet: CopperCorp Resources (TSXV: CPER) released final assay results from hole JDD008 at its Jukes copper project in Tasmania: 12.0 metres grading 0.54% copper, 0.14 g/t gold and 0.89 g/t silver from 92.0 metres depth, including 3.0 metres at 0.85% copper. True widths undetermined. Simultaneously, the company announced an A$100,000 Tasmanian Government Drilling Grant from Mineral Resources Tasmania — a direct subsidy supporting copper exploration on the island. The government backing signals Tasmania's strategy to attract copper-focused capital during a high-price environment (~$6.56/lb LME copper). For TSX-V investors, Tasmania-hosted copper projects remain underrepresented in the exploration cycle relative to BC and Nevada; the grant defrays Phase 2 drill costs and validates the project's standing with regulators.

headline: TOTAL METALS (TSXV: TT) FIRST HOLE HITS PURDEX QUARTZ VEINS AT HIGH LAKE — ONTARIO GOLD PROJECT ADVANCING TO ASSAY
snippet: Total Metals Corp. (TSXV: TT) reported that the first hole targeting the Purdex Zone at its High Lake high-grade gold project in Northwestern Ontario intersected the targeted quartz vein structures associated with historic high-grade gold mineralization. RC drilling is continuing across multiple priority targets identified by geophysics and surface sampling; assay results are pending. High Lake sits in the Northwestern Ontario gold belt that has historically hosted multi-million-ounce deposits, and the Purdex Zone represents the first systematic drill test of the project's highest-priority structural corridor since Total Metals acquired the property. The visual confirmation of targeted quartz veins in the first hole is the stage-gate that typically confirms the geological model — setting up a potentially significant assay release in the coming weeks for a company with a small market cap and tight share structure.

headline: CHINA'S NOVEMBER EXPORT CONTROLS TO TEST WESTERN RARE EARTH REFINING AMBITIONS — LYNAS, ILUKA, ENERGY FUELS FACE SUPPLY CHAIN RISK
snippet: A Fastmarkets analysis argues that China's October 2025 export control suspension expiring November 10 is the real test of whether Western rare earth refining and recycling ambitions are durable: if the suspension lapses, every non-Chinese manufacturer using Chinese-origin REE inputs in products traded with China must navigate MOFCOM case-by-case licensing — a compliance burden potentially affecting Lynas' mixed rare earth carbonate supply to Solvay, Iluka's Eneabba offtake logistics, and Energy Fuels' feedstock chain from Australia and Madagascar. The piece distinguishes this broader supply-chain risk from simple 'China blocks REE exports' framing — the mechanism targets the processing and downstream industrial supply chain rather than mine output directly. Market participants have largely priced in another suspension extension (the 'truce assumption'), making any non-renewal a significant negative surprise for Western defence and EV supply chains positioned around that assumption.

headline: URA ETF SLIDES TO NEW 52-WEEK LOWS AS AI-TECH SELLOFF SPREADS — SPOT URANIUM $89/LB STEADY WHILE EQUITIES PRICE DEEPER FEAR
snippet: The Global X Uranium ETF (URA) fell an additional 5.6% on November 2, 2026, pushing the fund through its prior 52-week low near $35.30 to an estimated $33.35 and extending its year-to-date loss to approximately 39% — a decline far in excess of the spot uranium price, which remains stable near $89–90/lb. The selloff stems primarily from AI/tech-sector margin calls spilling across the commodity equity complex rather than any change in uranium demand fundamentals: nuclear's role in powering data center buildout remains unchanged, long-term contract prices are holding near $70–75/lb, and the Lotus Resources first uranium shipment from Malawi this morning underscored that physical production is advancing as planned. The disconnect between spot uranium (~$89/lb) and equity-implied uranium pricing in URA is now at an extreme not seen since the 2022 uranium equity bear market trough — a setup that historically preceded the sector's strongest multi-year recoveries, though macro headwinds (Fed hike risk, tech selloff) remain unresolved.

headline: JUNIOR GOLD MINERS' MOST BINARY WEEK IN YEARS: GDXJ AT TWO-YEAR RELATIVE LOWS WITH MIDTERMS TUESDAY AND PAYROLLS FRIDAY
snippet: An FXEmpire analysis notes that junior gold miners (GDXJ) are approaching the November 3 midterms and November 6 nonfarm payrolls print at two-year relative lows versus gold itself — priced at the lowest gold-per-resource-ounce multiple since the 2018 bear market. The framework: if payrolls Friday comes in weak (consensus 68,000 jobs; a sub-40K print is the gold-bullish scenario), GDXJ's leveraged beta to gold means it would likely outperform the metal 2:1 or better on an algorithmic short-covering rally. If payrolls beats and gold breaks below the $3,750 Fibonacci support, GDXJ accelerates lower. The article frames this week as uniquely high-asymmetry for retail investors: the 11% October decline in gold (and the near-20% October decline in GDXJ) has created the kind of extreme sentiment reading and technical positioning that historically sets up the sharpest short-term recoveries in junior gold stocks — but only if the macro catalyst (payrolls) cooperates. Positioning sizing, not direction, is the key decision this week.
